page: Amazon Web Services t4g.xlarge is a burstable performance instance powered by custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, this server features 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs with a single thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the t4g.xlarge delivers moderate compute capabilities with notable performance tradeoffs. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieved average tier results with a single-core score of 1519.58 and a multi-core score of 6011.97. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for uncached large block reads at 66.09 GB/sec and writes at 32.48 GB/sec, though cached small block reads are relatively weak at 233.41 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates weaker performance in complex computational tasks, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 885.0 and a multi-core score of 3046.0. Cryptographic and decompression workloads also rank lower, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 541.1 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 6.43 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t4g.xlarge leverages the ARM64 architecture to offer a lower-cost entry point for workloads that do not require continuous maximum CPU utilization. Because it uses a burstable CPU allocation model, it is designed to accumulate CPU credits during idle periods to handle occasional spikes in demand. This resource profile is suitable for lightweight database operations, where it achieves an average Passmark database score of 2582.44, as well as basic web serving with 4.66 GB/sec static throughput and Redis caching with 4.28 million SET operations per second. It is less suitable for intensive tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, or LLM inference, where benchmarks show poor to weak performance.
description: Amazon Web Services t4g.xlarge is a burstable ARM64 instance powered by a 2.5 GHz AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 4 physical cores, 4 vCPUs, and 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on a 1 Gbps baseline network speed. Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities for standard compute and memory tasks, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6011.97 and average uncached memory write speeds of 32.48 GB/sec. However, it exhibits weaker results in complex processing, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 885.0. Utilizing a burstable CPU allocation model, the t4g.xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads with variable resource demands. It is best suited for lightweight database operations, basic web serving, and caching services rather than continuous high-compute tasks.
